What you'll do

We're hiring a Sales Enablement Specialist in Sales Operations to own the Sales Academy, from onboarding through a three-month ramp and ongoing enablement. You'll build its curriculum, performance measurement and AI-powered app so new hires can turn learning into sales results.

- Design the full ramp journey. Own the 30/60/90-day curriculum: product, ICP, sales methodology, tools and processes; then live calling, outbound sequences, pipeline generation and first deals; finally full quota accountability, ramp certification and graduation.

- Create training that stays current. Build playbooks, videos, reference guides, battle cards and interactive modules tailored to roles and markets. Extend enablement beyond onboarding through product launches, tool rollouts and messaging updates.

- Validate learning at every milestone. Design quizzes, practical evaluations and certification checkpoints. Define ramp benchmarks, report progress and flag at-risk new hires early so sales leaders can intervene.

- Connect learning to sales performance. Unify module completion, test scores and certifications with activity, pipeline and conversion metrics in new-hire scorecards. Report knowledge absorption trends, performance correlations and curriculum gaps to Sales leadership.

- Build a self-service Academy app. Create a central hub where new hires access learning paths, complete modules and assessments, and track progress, while sales leaders monitor ramp performance in real time.

- Personalize learning with AI. Use performance patterns to adapt learning paths, surface at-risk indicators and generate coaching suggestions. Own the app roadmap and ongoing improvements.

- Support reliable HubSpot administration. Handle account assignments, reassignments and territory or segment changes. Resolve ownership disputes while maintaining accurate account data.

- Maintain the Sales book of business. Own uploads and ongoing maintenance in HubSpot, ensuring accurate ownership and segmentation. Monitor and report adherence to assigned accounts and operational workflows.

How you'll work

You'll partner with Sales leadership and subject matter experts to turn real examples, strong call recordings and proven plays into training. Run end-of-cohort retrospectives with new hires and their sales leaders to improve the Academy.

Build with AI and no-code/low-code tools without depending on engineering resources, connecting HubSpot, Amplemarket and Slack data with learning progress. Use that evidence to prioritize app and curriculum improvements.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements for the role. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

jobs.description:
This is an in-office position, where you are expected to be in the office 5 days a week, from 9:00am - 5:00pm, with 2 days a month remote.

Mercury is looking for a Workplace Experience Specialist to bring our culture to life in our New York office through the operations of daily life in the space. This role owns the day-to-day office experience for our NYC team, ensuring that the environment people walk into each day reflects Mercury's thoughtful approach to design, quality, and connection. Our offices are where teams build relationships, solve difficult problems together, and experience the culture that makes working here meaningful.

In addition to running the daily experience, this role will support the cultural moments that punctuate the year: monthly office events, onsites hosted in NYC, and annual celebrations. You'll join a team that creates thoughtful, memorable moments for our employees with the same care we put into our products, and you'll partner closely with the broader People team, IT, and Finance on the larger operational pieces. Because our team is lean, your impact will be immediate — you'll set the tone for how Mercury's New York hub feels to the people in it.

What You'll Do

- Serve as the on-site presence and cultural ambassador for the NYC office every day, welcoming employees, guests, candidates, and visiting teammates.

- Own the daily operations of the space — lunch, kitchen, supply stocking, incoming/outgoing mail and deliveries, and visitor management — acting as the first point of contact for office questions and requests, resolving what you can and escalating what needs a broader fix.

- Keep the office beautiful, organized, and aligned with Mercury’s aesthetic.

- Shape a distinct in-office culture by listening to employee feedback and thoughtfully balancing individual requests with team needs, resources, and the overall workplace experience.

- Own monthly office events from concept through execution, building a program of gatherings that reflects Mercury’s culture and draws the local team in.

- Manage relationships with onsite vendors (cleaning, catering, snacks, plants, building maintenance) and track facilities and building requests to resolution, operating within your office budget.

- Set up desks, meeting rooms, and AV for new hires, guests, and visiting teams, and own the basics of office access and safety (badges, visitor sign-in, emergency procedures).

- Support the planning and execution of onsites and company events hosted in the NYC space, as well as broader employee experience initiatives — from All Hands and virtual events to merch production and cultural programs.

- Identify and lead improvements to office spaces, systems, and services to meet the evolving needs of a growing team.

- Communicate office updates, event invitations, and reminders clearly to the local team.

What Makes You a Great Fit

- Excited to be in office M-F, 9:00am - 5:00pm

- 2-3+ years of experience in office management.

- Genuine warmth with people and an instinct for anticipating what someone needs before they ask.

- Exceptional attention to detail and the organization to keep a dozen small threads moving without dropping any.

- Sound judgment about what to solve yourself and what to escalate with a little guidance from your manager, and the initiative to act without waiting to be asked.

- A refined eye for design and a deep appreciation for how a well-considered space makes people feel.

- Clear, friendly written communication across Slack, email, and signage.

- A collaborative team player who proactively asks for and acts on feedback, and pitches in on team activities beyond your core responsibilities when the opportunity comes up.

- NYC-based, with the expectation that you’re in the office every day — this role is on-site and hands-on by design, including moving boxes, resetting furniture, and being on your feet. Ability to lift 25 pounds if needed.

- Curiosity about people and what makes a space feel special.
